title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, Internal Tools
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document is the canonical company handbook reference for working at Redwood. It consolidates key information on our culture and ways of working, role and career ladder guidance, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding process, and the primary internal tools new and existing employees should know. Use this page as the single source of truth for people-ops owned policies and onboarding checklists.

1) Working at Redwood — culture & policies

- Mission alignment: We prioritize engineering-first development of inference; every role is encouraged to connect daily work to customer outcomes (latency, reliability, cost).
- Ways of working: asynchronous-first, documented decisions, weekly team rituals. Core collaboration hours: 10:00-16:00 local timezone for cross-functional teams.
- Remote & office policy: Redwood is remote-first with regional hubs. Employees are expected to attend team offsites twice per year.
- Time off: Flexible PTO with recommended minimum of 15 business days per year; managers should approve leaves in 3-5 business days.

2) Roles & career ladders (summary)

We maintain level descriptions and competencies for our major functions. Below are concise ladders and expectations; the full leveling guide is linked in the appendix.

- Engineering (IC ladder): E1 (new grad) -> E2 (individual contributor) -> E3 (senior) -> E4 (staff) -> E5 (principal). Key axes: impact, technical breadth, mentoring, architecture.
- Product: PM1 -> PM2 -> PM3 -> PM4 with similar axes: product outcome, cross-functional influence, metrics ownership.
- SRE/Infra: SRE1 -> SRE2 -> SRE3 -> SRE4 focused on SLO ownership, incident leadership, automation.
- Design, Research, Sales, Customer Success follow comparable leveling patterns with function-specific competencies.

Leveling quick reference (example table):

| Level | Years (typical) | Core expectations | Promotion signals |
|-------|-----------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| E2    | 1-3             | Delivers projects end-to-end; writes maintainable code | Repeated delivery, positive peer feedback |
| E3    | 3-6             | Architects subsystems; mentors 1-2 engineers | Leads cross-team projects, system design reviews |
| E4    | 6+              | Sets technical direction for a domain; influences roadmap | Significant customer/scale impact, org-wide influence |

Promotion process: manager calibration, written promotion packet (one-pager + examples), peer reviews, and people-ops signoff. Timelines vary; typical review cycle is quarterly.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

- Healthcare: comprehensive medical, dental, vision for employees and dependents (US & EU plans vary by region).
- Retirement: 401(k) with company match for US employees; local equivalents in other geographies.
- Equity: standard option grants at hire plus periodic refresh grants tied to role and performance.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (flexible top-up for managers).
- Learning & development: $2,000 annual learning stipend, conference budget by role.
- Wellness: monthly wellness stipend, mental health counseling through EAP.
- Office & remote: home office stipend on hire, co-working budget for those near hubs.

Benefit enrollment: new hires receive an enrollment packet during offer acceptance; benefits staff are on hand during the first week for questions.

4) Hiring & interview process (high-level)

We strive for predictable, inclusive, and fast hiring cycles. Typical steps:

1. Requisition & role profile created by hiring manager and approved by recruiting and finance.
2. Sourcing & resume screen (1-2 weeks).
3. Recruiter phone screen for fit and logistics (30-45 minutes).
4. Technical/functional interview loop (2-4 interviews, includes coding/design/behavioral).
5. Final bar-raiser interview and hiring committee review.
6. Offer, background check, and reference checks.

Target timeline: 4-6 weeks from first screen to offer for most IC roles. Hiring manager responsibilities: provide interviewers, calibration notes, and strong feedback within 72 hours of interviews.

Inclusive interviewing guidance (required reading for interviewers): prepare consistent rubrics, avoid closed questions about protected characteristics, and provide clear written feedback using the rubric.

5) New hire onboarding overview

Goal: enable new hires to make their first meaningful contribution within 30 days and take full ownership of role responsibilities within 90 days.

Day 0-7 (pre-start & week 1):
- Complete HR paperwork and benefits enrollment.
- IT provisioning: laptop, account access, MFA, VPN.
- Introduction meetings with manager and buddy assignment.
- First-week orientation session by people-ops.

Week 2-4:
- Shadowing and small onboarding tasks (bug fixes, doc updates).
- 1:1s with cross-functional peers (SRE, product, security).
- Complete role-specific training modules in the learning portal.

30/60/90 plan: New hires and managers should co-author a 30/60/90 plan covering objectives, success metrics, and checkpoints.

Onboarding checklist (numbered):
1. Verify hardware receipt and workspace set-up.
2. Confirm access to GitHub, Jira, Slack, and the Redwood Console.
3. Complete mandatory security training within 14 days.
4. Meet cross-functional stakeholders and set initial goals.
5. Deliver first scoped contribution and update the onboarding tracker.

6) Internal tools & access (quick guide)

Primary tools and purpose:
- Slack: company communication. Join channels: #announcements, #eng-all, team-specific channels.
- GitHub: code, PR process. Use branch naming: team/short-description (e.g., runtime/batch-optim).
- Jira: issue tracking and sprint work. Follow our issue templates (see appendix).
- Redwood Console: product dashboards, per-route latency/cost. Access via SSO.
- rdw-cli: internal CLI for environment setup and lightweight ops. Example setup: 

```bash
# Install rdw-cli
pip install redwood-cli
# Authenticate (SSO will open a browser)
rdw auth login
# List assigned projects
rdw projects list
```

- VPN & Bastion: Access to private deployments requires Duo MFA and the corporate VPN. Example SSH pattern: 

```bash
ssh -i ~/.ssh/redwood_key ubuntu@bastion.redwood.internal
```

Access request process:
- Submit an access request ticket via the Helpdesk portal with justification and owner (manager). Access expires after 180 days unless renewed. For sensitive customer environments, raise a request with security approval (see security-and-compliance/req-template).

7) Day 0-30 onboarding checklist (owner and due dates)

| Item | Owner | Due |
|------|-------|-----|
| Laptop & peripherals shipped | IT Operations | Day -1 |
| Accounts provisioned (SSO, GitHub, Jira) | IT Operations | Day 0 |
| Security training completed | New hire | Day 14 |
| Buddy assigned and 1:1 schedule | Hiring manager | Day 1 |
| First scoped contribution merged | New hire + Manager | Day 30 |

8) Escalations, ownership & contacts

- People-ops (onboarding & benefits): people-ops@redwood.com
- IT support: it-support@redwood.com (helpdesk ticket required)
- Security: security@redwood.com (for access to restricted tooling)
- Recruiting: recruiting@redwood.com

9) Appendix & links

- Full leveling guide: /confluence/company-handbook/leveling-guide-2024 (internal link)
- Interview rubric templates: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/interview-rubrics
- Onboarding tracker template: /confluence/company-handbook/onboarding-tracker-template
- Benefits FAQ and enrollment forms: /confluence/company-handbook/benefits-enrollment-2025

If you are a manager or buddy and notice missing items or gaps in this document, please open a PR against the handbook repo or contact people-ops@redwood.com.
